subject: Vendor portal onboarding: artifact catalog & proof-of-possession (Aurora Health)
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Garcia <lisa.garcia@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Vendor portal onboarding: artifact catalog & proof-of-possession (Aurora Health)

Hi Lisa —

Thanks again for the call this morning. To get Aurora set up in Vendr and finish the minimal evidence bundle for procurement, we need a short artifact catalog / proof-of-possession manifest from your side plus a couple of clarifying Qs:

- Preferred delivery: Vendr portal upload or S3 pre-signed delivery? (we can accept either)
- Primary contact for SOC 2 follow-up (name + email).
- Any restrictions on sharing the SOC 2 summary with our security review board?

Attached is a template manifest we typically use (redwood_evidence_manifest_aurora_20280730.csv) — fill the rows for the items you’ll provide and mark which artifacts are sensitive. If you’d like us to upload on your behalf to Vendr, we can coordinate a short SSO connection.

Next steps from Redwood: Mina will validate the manifest against our SIG mapping and Priyom will prepare the portal upload checklist. If you can get the manifest back today or early tomorrow, we can target a portal completion by Wednesday.

Thanks —

Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: redwood_evidence_manifest_aurora_20280730.csv (CSV template)
From: Lisa Garcia <lisa.garcia@aurorahealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Security Team <security@aurorahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 10:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vendor portal onboarding: artifact catalog & proof-of-possession (Aurora Health)

Vanessa —

Thanks for the summary and the template. Quick answers inline:

- Delivery: Vendr preferred (our security team likes the portal audit logs), but we can do an S3 handoff if needed.
- SOC 2 contact: Aaron Kim, aaron.kim@aurorahealth.com (he owns external audits).
- Sharing restrictions: SOC 2 summary (Type II) is ok to share with vendor security teams; full report requires an NDA.

We’ll start populating the CSV. Two small asks from our side: (1) can you confirm retention expectations for artifacts once uploaded? (2) is there a recommended redaction process for customer data in logs?

—Lisa
Lisa Garcia
Vendor Ops, Aurora Health
lisa.garcia@aurorahealth.com

Subject: Re: Vendor portal onboarding: artifact catalog & proof-of-possession (Aurora Health)

Lisa —

Thanks — perfect. Quick answers to your asks:

1) Retention: Redwood keeps evidence artifacts in our staging S3 for 90 days by default after upload to a vendor portal, unless otherwise negotiated in the contract. If Aurora needs a different TTL, we can include that in the Dedicated/Private play.

2) Redaction: For logs we recommend (a) remove PII at source, (b) supply redacted excerpts with a short mapping file explaining fields removed, or (c) provide a redaction script snippet. We do not need full raw logs unless specifically requested by an auditor.

I’ve attached a filled manifest v0.1 with the items we expect (marked tentative): redwood_evidence_manifest_aurora_20280730.csv. If you’d like us to connect your security team to Vendr SSO, share an admin email and we’ll send the SSO invite.

Vanessa

Attachments: redwood_evidence_manifest_aurora_20280730.csv (filled v0.1), soc2-type2-2027-summary.pdf (summary)
